platform: macOS 26.5 (25F71), arm64, Apple Silicon; debug build with the embedded frontend, isolated test mode (ADR 0003, macOS amendment), WKWebView driven through the test bridge (src-tauri/src/test_bridge.rs)
method: One isolated instance, one conversation created from the welcome screen on a scratch workspace under the run's temp folder (itself below /var/folders, a symlinked root on macOS). The Files tab was driven in the page (element.click() on rows and buttons, as in the Windows record); files were created, renamed and deleted on disk by the harness with Node's fs, never through the app.

limits: macOS defect holding the ticket at ◐: a folder over the 200-entry bound lists 200 entries taken in read_dir order and only then sorted (src-tauri/src/files.rs, list: the loop stops pushing at max_entries before entries.sort_by). NTFS returns names in order, so on Windows these are the first 200 by name; APFS returns them in hash order, so on macOS the view shows an arbitrary 200, sorted, under a note that says 'the first 200 entries' (measured: 75 of the 200 shown are among the first 200 by name), and an entry renamed on disk may never appear after Refresh (the Windows replay of the rename inside the 550-entry folder fails; the same rename in a folder under the bound appears). Not data loss, not security. Fix direction (not applied): collect the names, sort, then truncate.
Open in app (the system default handler, LaunchServices here) was not clicked: it would open an app on the user's desktop; the Windows record did not click it either.
The watcher and symlink checks go beyond the Windows record (ticket text); they are recorded, not closing criteria.
